chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to him, 'I have some wealth due from one of the al-Hasaniyyun, and its collection has tired me, and there has been some speech between me and him, and I do not fear that something which would cause me distress may occur between me and him regarding that.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'This is not the way for debt collection, but when you go to him, prolong your sitting and maintain silence.' The man said, 'So I did that only for a little while, until I took my wealth.'

key_terms.الْحَسَنِيِّينَ: The descendants of Hasan (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for collecting a debt without causing conflict?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific etiquette for debt collection, advising the debtor to sit quietly and speak little to avoid the emotional escalation that often accompanies verbal disputes. This approach highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and emotional restraint (*hilm*) in financial transactions, ensuring that the righting of a wrong does not become a source of further spiritual or social harm. The man’s quick success after applying this advice underscores the practical efficacy of maintaining composure and dignity in interpersonal dealings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man said to him, ‘There is some wealth for me upon one of the two Husayns, and its collection has tired me, and there has flowed some speech between me and him, and I am not secure that there would flow between me and him with regards to that what would be distressing for me’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘This is not the way for the collection, but when you go over to him, prolong your sitting and adopt calmness’. The man said, ‘So I did that only for a little while, until I received my wealth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu’ manner has narrated the following: “He (the narrator) has said that

a man once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘A man of Al- Husayniy people owes me a certain amount. Asking him for payment has become tiring for me. We had an argument about it and I am afraid something may happen between us that will make me sad.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘This is not a proper manner of asking for payment. When you go to him next time sit with him for a long time and remain quiet.’ The man has said, ‘I followed the instruction and shortly thereafter I received full payment.’”
